markdown:
## Why Career Pathing Matters

Lack of growth opportunity is one of the reasons people commonly give for leaving a job. A visible path will not keep everyone, but it makes the conversation about growth concrete. This article quotes no retention figures, because we have not cited a source for any.

### Building Career Frameworks

#### Step 1: Define Levels

Create clear levels for every function.

*Illustrative example only. Titles, scope and experience ranges are placeholders to adapt, not a benchmark.*

| Level | Title | Scope | Typical experience |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Junior Engineer | Task execution | Early career |
| L2 | Engineer | Feature ownership | Some years in role |
| L3 | Senior Engineer | Project leadership | Several years |
| L4 | Staff Engineer | Cross-team technical leadership | Substantial experience |
| L5 | Principal Engineer | Org-wide technical strategy | Extensive experience |

#### Step 2: Define Competencies Per Level

For each level, specify expectations across dimensions:

- Technical skills
- Scope of impact
- Leadership and influence
- Communication
- Business acumen

#### Step 3: Create Assessment Criteria

Make promotion decisions transparent:

- Skills demonstration (projects, presentations, reviews)
- Peer feedback
- Manager assessment
- Calibration across teams to ensure consistency

#### Step 4: Enable Multiple Paths

Not everyone wants to be a manager. Create parallel tracks:

- Individual contributor track (deep technical expertise)
- Management track (people leadership)
- Hybrid track (technical plus some management)

### Career Conversations

Managers should hold career development conversations regularly, for example quarterly:

- "Where do you see yourself in two years?"
- "What skills do you want to develop?"
- "What experiences would help you grow?"
- "How can I support your development?"
- "Are there projects or teams you are interested in?"

### Internal Mobility Programs

Strong internal mobility can reduce external hiring cost and build institutional knowledge. Enable it through:

- An internal job board, with roles posted internally first
- Cross-functional project assignments
- Rotation programs
- Internal mentoring across teams

### Measuring Career Pathing Impact

Track these against your own baseline rather than a general target:

- Internal promotion rate
- Time in role before promotion
- Internal mobility rate (share of roles filled internally)
- Employee satisfaction with growth opportunities (pulse survey)
- Voluntary turnover by level
